newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-EU wrong to reintroduce grain subsidies - AWB.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-EU wrong to reintroduce grain subsidies - AWB.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) on Friday criticised the European Union's (EU) decision to subsidise grain exports.
"It's the wrong signal at the wrong time," AWB managing director John Lawrenson said in a statement.
Although the size of subsidies were relatively small, the timing of the announcement was particularly disturbing, he said.

The EU Commission announced subsidies of up to A$6 a tonne on 160,000 tonnes of wheat destined for African, European and Caribbean nations last week and was expected to announce further subsidised sales, Lawrenson said in a statement.
"It's just a week or so since the EU Commissioners were taxing any grain exports in an attempt to keep grain prices within Europe under control," Lawrenson said.
"Now they're subsidising exports again. That is particularly confusing to a market that is already extremely volatile," he said.

The international market expected the EU to export close to seven million tonnes of wheat this year, he said. "If it does that then its stocks of wheat will grow by about half a million tonnes. Now that it has introduced subsidies into the equation the market is asking how much and how far," he said.
The EU decision was puzzling because the underlying market fundamentals had not changed. World stocks of grain were still very tight and the market was particularly volatile, he said.
It had been almost nine months since the U.S. and EU offered subsidised grain for sale, he said.
"The world has learned to live without subsidies and present market conditions make it very dangerous to reintroduce them," he said.
